pl-l2d44c1-d1e108.summary: Introduces the question whether the power of sinning is from God or from ourselves.
claims: The question is whether the power of sinning is from God or from us.

pl-l2d44c1-d1e111.summary: Presents the opponents' view: the power of acting rightly is from God, but the power of sinning is from us or the devil, by analogy with good and bad will. Supported by Augustine (via Prosper) that the beginning of good will is divinely given and neither devil nor angel can regain it by themselves.
claims: Opponents hold that power for good is from God, power for evil is from humans or the devil.
Opponents argue by analogy from will to power.

pl-l2d44c1-d1e116.summary: Counter-thesis: many testimonies of the saints show that the power of evil is from God, from whom all power derives.
claims: The power of evil is from God, source of all power.

pl-l2d44c1-d1e120.summary: Scriptural proof: Romans 13 and Christ's words to Pilate show that all power, including power over evil ends, is given from above; the claim must cover evil power as well as good.
claims: 'No power but from God' applies to evil power as well as good.

pl-l2d44c1-d1e126.summary: Augustine's distinction: malice has the desire to harm from itself but the power to harm only from God. Illustrated with the devil's request to God in Job, and Proverbs, Job, and Hosea on rulers; God justly uses power given to the devil to make the just his own.
claims: Desire to harm can come from the human mind; power to harm only from God.
God uses the power granted to the devil for the benefit of the just.

pl-l2d44c1-d1e131.summary: Gregory: what is blameworthy is the swelling pride that abuses power, not the ordering of power, which God gives; what belongs to us is the wicked action, not the just power.
claims: Power is given by God and is not itself culpable; its proud misuse is.
Condemnation falls on the evil act, not the power.

pl-l2d44c1-d1e134.summary: Concludes that power of good or evil is from God alone, by a justice that may be hidden from the observer.
claims: No power of good or evil exists except from God's just ordering.

pl-l2d44c1.summary: Lombard argues against those who hold that the power of sinning comes from humans or the devil rather than God, maintaining through scriptural and patristic authorities that all power, even the power to do evil, is from God, while the wickedness lies in the will and its abuse.
claims: The power to sin or harm comes from God, though the will to do so does not.
Evil is located in the elation of the will, not in the order of power.
The analogy between bad will and bad power, which would exclude God from the latter, fails.
